findings.description: Several canonical current-state surfaces state without qualification that 'GOALS.md criteria 5, 6, and 8 are met as shipped', which overclaims criterion 6. The project's own limitations record says criterion 6 is only partial: docs/limitations.md line 32 ('Met for render/publication; partial for provider fetches', item F1) and PLANS.md task 7.6 status (line 2843) and README.md line 562 ('criterion 6 is met for render and publication but only partial for provider fetches'). The unqualified claim survives in README.md:24, PLANS.md:5, PLANS.md:179 (Milestone 7 row), docs/architecture.md:3, docs/implementation-readiness.md:5, and docs/changelog.md:2060/2267. This is an internal contradiction between canonical surfaces, not a stylistic gap. It does not block the phase because the accurate status is recorded and the Phase 7 acceptance criterion 3 (changed/unchanged metadata scenarios) is genuinely met, but a reader of the top-level status can incorrectly conclude that the 'avoid unnecessary API requests' goal is fully satisfied.
evidence: README.md:24 unqualified 'criteria 5, 6, and 8 are therefore met as shipped' vs README.md:562 qualified criterion 6
PLANS.md:5 and PLANS.md:179 unqualified vs PLANS.md:2843 'criterion 6 is met for render and publication but only partial for provider fetches'
docs/limitations.md:32 status 'Met for render/publication; partial for provider fetches' with item F1
findings.recommended_action: Qualify the criterion-6 statements on the current-state surfaces (README project status, PLANS.md Project Status + Milestone 7 row, architecture status line, implementation-readiness status line, changelog Phase 7 status) with the same 'render/publication met, provider fetches partial (F1)' wording already used in docs/limitations.md. No code change required.

findings.description: ADR-012 states authentication failures return a bounded 401 'with no body', but live webhook 401 responses carry the ASP.NET Core [ApiController] application/problem+json ProblemDetails body (type/title/status/traceId). No secret or sensitive detail is reflected; the behaviour is accurately recorded in docs/limitations.md D1 (task 7.4 reviewer finding 7.4-R2). The divergence is documented, not silent, but the ADR text is now inaccurate.
findings.recommended_action: Track for a future ADR-012 clarification (or suppress the framework body so the implemented behaviour matches the ADR). Non-blocking for V1: no leakage, documented.

findings.description: ArtworkSubjectGate.Gates is a process-local static ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> keyed by item id + image surface with no idle eviction or LRU bound; one semaphore is retained per distinct (item, surface) for process lifetime. Growth is bounded in practice by the number of distinct Jellyfin library items and is not attacker-controllable nor a log/state path. Recorded as task 7.4 reviewer finding 7.4-R1 and docs/limitations.md D2.
findings.recommended_action: Optional post-V1 hardening: drop idle entries on the lifecycle drain or add an LRU bound. Not a V1 requirement.

findings.description: scripts/pack-release.cs validates that the staging directory exists and is non-empty but does not validate the expected release file set, so an out-of-band direct invocation can pack an incomplete archive with exit 0 (task 7.5 reviewer finding 7.5-F1). In addition, a failed ./build.sh package leaves artifacts/staging behind because the trailing cleanup is not trapped under set -e (finding 7.5-F2). Neither is reachable through the documented pipeline (MSBuild Copy fails first; artifacts/ is gitignored) and both were explicitly recorded as not-required.
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening: assert the expected file set in the packer and use trap-based staging cleanup. Not required for V1.

findings.description: docs/limitations.md did not record that the final byte-reproducible 567,856-byte artifact was not itself live-verified end-to-end; task 7.8's live run used the earlier 568,004-byte package (task 7.6 reviewer finding 7.6-R1). This phase review independently closed the substantive gap: it built the current artifact (SHA-256 bd10b9b6bf5d31049082d27625b18ba127eb6e2860a454fe2d3c35ccebaaee51, 567,856 bytes), installed exactly that archive as /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0 on the pinned host, and verified live end-to-end publication (movie image/png 5,977 B SHA-256 e7db5182... and episode image/png 8,154 B SHA-256 54f937c1..., both equal to the persisted ActiveImageIdentity; 0 [FTL]/InvalidCastException; source posters byte-unchanged). Only the documentation note remains.

findings.recommended_action: Add a one-line verification note to docs/limitations.md recording that the current byte-reproducible artifact was live-verified end-to-end by the Phase 7 review; no code action.

summary: Phase 7 (Testing & release, Milestone 7) is complete and Gate 7 is satisfied. All eight tasks in the authoritative order 7.1, 7.2, 7.7, 7.3, 7.8, 7.4, 7.5, 7.6 are complete, committed in dependency order, and each carries committed worker and reviewer reports plus an orchestration record; the two tasks added mid-phase (7.7, 7.8) are documented in PLANS.md with their dependency positions and are legitimate resolutions of confirmed BLOCKER findings, not scope invention. The two release blockers were independently reproduced as genuinely fixed: (7.2-F1) installing the current release archive as /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, letting the plugin write state, and restarting preserves the versioned install folder and loads exactly one plugin with state at /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags and no PluginsPath/ArrTags folder (plus a live authenticated DELETE /Plugins/<guid>/0.1.0.0 -> 204 that drained and removed the relocated state root); (7.3-F1) the package contains no SkiaSharp.dll/libSkiaSharp.so, and the same archive published movie and episode badges through the real host IProviderManager.SaveImage with 0 [FTL]/InvalidCastException, served by GET /Items/{id}/Images/Primary as image/png whose SHA-256 equals the persisted ActiveImageIdentity (e7db5182.../54f937c1...), with source posters byte-unchanged. Build/test/artifact independently reproduced: clean rebuild 0 warnings/0 errors; default suite Failed 0/Passed 1218/Skipped 60/Total 1278; host-guarded suite 1234/44/1278; two clean ./build.sh package runs produced the identical SHA-256 bd10b9b6bf5d31049082d27625b18ba127eb6e2860a454fe2d3c35ccebaaee51 (567,856 bytes, 7 entries, no duplicate renderer runtime). ADR-014 and ADR-015 are coherent with the prior ADRs, ADR-010's partial supersession is recorded, and no ADR is silently contradicted. All GOALS.md success criteria and all five Phase 7 acceptance criteria are either genuinely met with evidence or accurately recorded as partial/contract-level/verification-limited in docs/limitations.md; the only substantive documentation defect is an overclaim of GOALS criterion 6 ('met as shipped') on several current-state surfaces that contradicts the project's own 'partial for provider fetches' record (MEDIUM). Remaining open items (7.4-R1/R2, 7.5-F1/F2, 7.6-R1/R2/R3) are non-blocking and are tracked in docs/limitations.md or PLANS.md; none prevents V1 release. All findings are documentation/precision/technical-debt items and none is a BLOCKER or HIGH.
